items.title: Smulyan interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2010
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Here’s some names I’ll lump together, which probably I shouldn’t, but guys like Pharoh Sanders, Patrick Gilmore — [INTERVIEWEE] John Gilmore.

ctx.x: It’s actually a perfect example of you play how you are. And you can’t hide. You can’t be different than you play. Your playing is a direct reflection of who you are as a person. And I tell my students, I say what comes in comes out. If nothing comes in, nothing is going to come out. So like I was saying before, the movies you watch, the books you read, everything that comes in, as a musician, is going to come out in your breath. It’s important. I mean Cannonball was a school teacher, right? So he was constantly…
